themes.note: Each base key is the day value; its -dark sibling is the lamp-lit value applied under prefers-color-scheme: dark (unless data-theme="light") and under data-theme="dark". Dark dims the book without inverting it: paper stays light sage under dark ink, and both themes declare color-scheme: light. cover-ink and cover-dim are shared. --focus equals --stamp in both themes.

narrative.overview:
The site is a Thai bank passbook (สมุดบัญชี) that belongs to one person and never leaves him, the same way the AI he builds never leaves the device. The page ground is the navy cover; every readable surface is a leaf of mint security paper printed with a faint guilloche wave; text is carbon-blue ink; and one vermilion teller-stamp red marks what has been verified and what missed. Projects are not cards: they are printed ledger entries in a ruled table, each dated by the month it was opened, with its proof figure, the condition that figure was measured under, and a count of cloud calls.

Density is that of a working document, not a brochure. Lines are ruled, figures are right-aligned and printed in a dot-matrix face, prose is set in one humanist sans that carries Thai and Latin as equals. There are no corners, no shadows and no glows. Depth is physical: the leaves are stacked, so the edges of the pages beneath show at the bottom-right of each sheet; the open spread folds into its gutter; and a darker back board, closed off by a double rule, ends the book.

Light theme is the passbook by day. Dark theme is the same book under a desk lamp: the cover drops to near-black navy and the paper dims to a deeper sage, but the pages stay paper — ink stays dark on light, and the paper keeps `color-scheme: light`. It is the same object in lower light, never an inverted screen.
keyCharacteristics: Navy cover as page ground, mint guilloche paper as every reading surface.
Ruled ledger lines instead of cards; square corners everywhere.
Anuphan for all prose and dates in EN and TH; Doto dot-matrix only for printed ledger figures.
One stamp red, reserved for verified marks, misses and focus.
No shadows, no glows; depth by stacked leaves, the gutter fold and cover/paper contrast.
Every figure carries its condition; every entry carries its opening month.

rules.name: The One Red Rule
rules.body: Stamp vermilion is the only saturated warm color. It means "verified", "missed" or "you are here" (focus). It never decorates, never fills a button, never colors a heading.

rules.name: The Two Surfaces Rule
rules.body: Content sits either on paper (ink colors) or on the cover (cover-ink colors). Never set paper ink on the cover or cover ink on paper.

rules.name: The Desk Lamp Rule
rules.body: Dark theme dims the book; it does not invert it. Paper stays a light sage under dark ink, the cover goes near-black, and every new token needs both a day and a lamp-lit value that keeps that relationship.

rules.name: The Guilloche Texture Rule
rules.body: Every paper surface carries the guilloche wave (`--guilloche-img`, a 160 × 24 px tile of three sine polylines in ink at 12% opacity, the same tile in both themes). It is a texture under text, not an ornament; never enlarge, recolor or animate it.

rules.name: The Printer Rule
rules.body: Doto is for what the ledger printed — proof figures, cloud counts, opened months, print times — and the demo's predicted letter. Never for prose, headings, labels or dates a person wrote (history periods are Anuphan).

rules.name: The Untracked Thai Rule
rules.body: Thai is never letter-spaced and never uppercased into tracking: every tracked label (column heads, block heads, stamp, brand) reverts to `letter-spacing: normal` under `lang="th"`.

rules.name: The Stacked Leaf Rule
rules.body: If a surface needs to read as separate or on top, change its material (cover vs paper vs paper-3), rule it, or lay it on offset paper edges; never lift it with a shadow.

rules.name: The One Fold Rule
rules.body: The only gradient is the gutter fold beside the spine. No other gradient, sheen or vignette belongs on paper or cover.

dos: Do set every readable surface on paper with the guilloche texture, and every frame element (bar, footer, back cover) on the cover.
Do give each major paper sheet its stacked leaf edges (paper-2 at 5px, paper-3 at 10px, 1px rule) instead of any shadow.
Do print every ledger figure in Doto with tabular numerals and put its measurement condition directly beneath it in faded ink.
Do date every ledger entry by its first-commit month (`JUN 2026` / `มิ.ย. 2569`).
Do set history and other written dates in Anuphan 600 with tabular figures.
Do separate rows and regions with rules (1px rule, 1.5px rule-strong) rather than boxes.
Do keep corners at 0px and buttons at 48px tall with 2px borders that invert on hover.
Do reserve stamp red for verified marks, misses and focus.
Do give Thai the same face, size and weight as English, and drop letter-spacing for Thai.
Do define both a day and a lamp-lit value for every new color token, keeping dark ink on light paper in both.
donts: Don't use cards, drop shadows, glows or blur on passbook surfaces.
Don't add gradients beyond the gutter fold.
Don't use Doto for prose, headings, labels or written dates.
Don't use stamp red as a fill, a heading color or decoration.
Don't invert the paper to dark in dark theme.
Don't let the email break anywhere but after the `@`.
Don't add kickers or eyebrow labels above headings.
Don't reintroduce the old dark dev-portfolio vocabulary: zinc greys, emerald glows, metric tiles, 3D heroes.
